Armed Conflict & Security
• Russian drones struck Kyiv’s Northern (Pivnichyi) Bridge, igniting a fireball, as Germany’s chancellor made an unannounced visit to the capital; Berlin remains Kyiv’s biggest donor. 
• Ethiopian federal forces retook Mekelle’s airport and asserted control of Tigray’s capital as TPLF leaders withdrew, signaling a major shift in the renewed conflict.
• Sudan’s army claims gains in North Kordofan, threatening RSF supply lines and recruitment routes amid a grinding war.
• Australian authorities are probing ties of a Flydubai co-pilot after an attempted hijacking en route to Israel; separately, debris was found from a small plane that vanished off the US coast.
• Families of Fox News journalists killed in Ukraine have sued the network, while Mexico said a joint “mirror” deployment with the US put troops on both sides of the Texas border.
Why it matters: Intensifying strikes in Ukraine, shifting battle lines in Ethiopia and Sudan, and heightened aviation-security concerns underscore a volatile global security environment with ripple effects for aid, diplomacy and regional stability.

Geopolitics & Diplomacy
• Brazil votes in a razor-tight, polarized presidential race between incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro, with polls showing a dead heat.
• Iran signaled the Strait of Hormuz will remain closed unless US conditions are met, raising stakes for energy security and regional diplomacy.
• The US announced its military withdrawal from Iraq is complete, ending a 23-year engagement that reshaped Middle East policy.
• Donald Trump’s midterm campaign blitz stirs debate over whether his rallies energize or fatigue voters, as Republicans weigh risks and rewards.
Why it matters: Democratic trajectories in Brazil, strategic chokepoints in the Gulf, and shifts in US force posture all shape global energy, markets and alliances ahead of a pivotal election season.

Climate & Environment
• A rare tornado hit Ulladulla, New South Wales, damaging property and downing trees amid a season of volatile weather.
• Drought is reshaping Europe: a French-Swiss lake has dried up and Hungarian paprika farmers are struggling after an exceptionally dry summer.
• This year’s record-strengthening El Niño is amplifying drought in some regions and floods in others, as rapid Pacific warming disrupts weather patterns.
• Cutting greenhouse gas emissions now could limit Antarctic ice loss and reduce sea-level rise this century; meanwhile, the UK reportedly dropped a wildfire preparedness plan despite rising risk.
Why it matters: Climate extremes are already altering ecosystems, economies and public safety, intensifying the urgency for mitigation and adaptation.

Society & Human Rights
• Tens of thousands protested across Spain after a housing bill failed in parliament, with organizers demanding emergency measures and warning of political fallout.
• France arrested around 5,000 people, mostly teens, as high school protests over overcrowding, teacher shortages and crumbling buildings spread nationwide.
• Cornell University pledged a “serious look” at Greek life following allegations a student was drugged and raped by fraternity members; the case has sparked widespread outrage.
• Ghana may curb preaching on public transport, reflecting tensions between religious expression and public order; in the US, a father and son were arrested over kratom-derived products linked to student deaths.
• Thousands of Glasgow council workers face “fire-and-rehire” pay cuts after union talks collapsed, highlighting labor tensions in public services.
Why it matters: Social strains from housing and education to campus safety and labor rights are testing institutions and could reshape political agendas.

Sports
• Max Verstappen won a rain-delayed F1 race in Sepang, taking Red Bull’s first victory of the year in a chaotic event; Mercedes’ George Russell retired.
• Natalia Silva captured the UFC women’s flyweight title by unanimous decision over China’s Wang Cong at UFC 332.
• Bosnia’s Edin Dzeko bid farewell to international football, drawing tributes after a storied career.
• Croatia captain Luka Modric called his team’s performance against England “catastrophic,” saying he was “ashamed.”
Why it matters: High-profile wins, shocks and farewells shape momentum across motorsport, MMA and football ahead of critical fixtures and title campaigns.
https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2026/10/4/red-bulls-verstappen-wins-rain-delayed-bahrain-gp-f1-race-in-sepang?traffic_source=rss https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/formula1/articles/c5n49zx3zlvwo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/mixed-martial-arts/articles/c670pzzzxgzeo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss https://www.aljazeera.com/video/newsfeed/2026/10/4/tributes-as-bosnian-football-star-edin-dzeko-retires?traffic_source=rss https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cwzrdm3lyk21o?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

Economy & Markets
• OPEC+ will keep November oil output quotas steady as Middle East conflict constrains supply; Iraq booked a VLCC to move 2 million barrels beyond Hormuz, signaling efforts to diversify routes.
• Traders eye contagion risks after a European government bond selloff evoked memories of the debt crisis.
• IPO momentum has cooled amid tepid demand and valuation concerns, with several listings paused.
• China shuttered a record 670-plus banks last year to shore up its financial system, as rating agencies warn smaller lenders remain a weak link.
• Policymakers and investors remain split on AI infrastructure growth: rural US data centers could get major tax breaks even as global communities push back on rising costs.
Why it matters: Energy supply discipline, fragile debt markets and uneven capital formation point to a more cautious global outlook as policymakers juggle growth, stability and tech-driven investment.

Health & Pandemic
• Pennsylvania is bracing for broader measles spread, reporting its fifth death and 943 cases across 39 counties, with uneven local public health capacity and low vaccination pockets compounding risk.
Why it matters: Resurgent vaccine-preventable diseases highlight the consequences of weakened public health infrastructure and eroding immunization coverage.
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/04/pennsylvania-health-officials-measles-outbreak

Artificial Intelligence
• An OpenAI safety employee resigned, alleging a “broken” culture, as reports of dozens of hacks targeting the company’s tools raise legal risks and potential lawsuits.
• Meta’s Muse agent is expanding shopping integrations with major retailers, while critics warn of growing privacy trade-offs as the system builds detailed user profiles.
• AI “agents” are proliferating in messaging, with startups and tech giants testing assistants for families, travel and work—and early lessons from reliability gaps.
• Capcom says it is preparing for a “future where we create games together with AI,” signaling deeper integration of AI into game development pipelines.
• Masayoshi Son’s AI ambitions are outgrowing SoftBank’s balance sheet, with third-party infrastructure partners stepping in to finance data center buildout.
Why it matters: Rapid AI deployment is colliding with governance, privacy and infrastructure constraints, forcing companies to balance innovation with safety, trust and capital needs.

Entertainment
• Saturday Night Live’s Dakota Johnson episode featured a Taylor Swift cameo, GOP satire in the cold open, and an explosive Turnstile musical debut.
• Tom McCarthy’s climate docudrama “A Statement” drew mixed reviews, with Paul Rudd reflecting on digital distraction and set discipline.
• Tom Cruise and Guillermo del Toro publicly backed the dark comedy “Digger” amid a tough opening frame and polarized reviews.
• Fashion month rolled on with major Spring 2027 ready-to-wear shows from Miu Miu, Lacoste, Alaïa and others.
• Legacy acts delivered big moments: AC/DC brought out Dave Grohl at MetLife, and Elton John thanked fans as he bids farewell on stage in Mexico City.
Why it matters: Cultural touchpoints from SNL to global runways and veteran tours shape public conversation and highlight the industry’s balancing act between nostalgia, experimentation and box-office realities.

Science & Technology
• Milt Windler, a NASA flight director who helped steer Apollo 13 safely home, died at 94, marking the loss of a key figure in human spaceflight history.
• Amazon Web Services, facing local pushback, said it no longer uses NDAs in data center negotiations as scrutiny of large-scale infrastructure grows.
• Researchers unveiled a reactor design that improves plastic feedstock synthesis using oxygen and electricity, revealing a “hidden variable” near electrodes that can make or break reactions.
• Astronomers suggest a nearby binary star system could host an Earth-sized planet in a temperate zone where liquid water may exist, bolstering prospects for habitable worlds in complex systems.
Why it matters: Infrastructure transparency, cleaner industrial chemistry and fresh paths to habitable exoplanets reflect how science and policy are reshaping technology’s footprint on Earth—and beyond.
https://arstechnica.com/space/2026/10/milt-windler-nasa-flight-director-who-helped-save-apollo-13-dies-at-94/ https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/03/amazon-responds-to-data-center-backlash-says-it-no-longer-uses-ndas/ https://phys.org/news/2026-09-reactor-plastic-feedstock-synthesis-oxygen.html https://phys.org/news/2026-09-qa-earth-planet-suns.html

Longevity & Anti-Aging
• A study reports induced neural stem cell conversion of human blood cells shows “epigenetic de-aging,” with fate acquisition occurring over a prolonged period.
Why it matters: Reprogramming blood cells toward neural stem-like states hints at regenerative avenues and biomarkers for reversing age-associated epigenetic changes.

Armed Conflict & Security.title: Friedrich Merz begins unannounced Kyiv visit as Russia continues strikes on Ukraine’s capital – Europe live
Armed Conflict & Security.text:
German chancellor tours city with president Zelenskyy after Moscow strikes city’s North Bridge this morning amid his arrivalGermany is Ukraine’s largest donor and has sent Kyiv more than €43.3 billion ($48.8 billion) since the war began, along with equipment and weapons.
 Zelenskyy thanked Merz for visiting the Ukrainian capital describing him as “A leader of a country that consistently demonstrates leadership in protecting the lives of Ukrainians from Russian strikes. 
 We are grateful for all the support, and today we are preparing decisions to give us in Ukraine, and all of Europe, greater capabilities to defend ourselves. There will be important agreements between Ukraine and Germany. Russia must be stopped together.”Zelenskyy in the past hour has been tweeting about the strikes and the German chancellor’s visit, thanking Merz for his support.
 On the Kyiv strike this morning he confirmed it had been a drone on the Northern Bridge (Pivnichnyi Bridge).
 He noted too a drone attack on a pharmaceutical warehouse in Sumy which killed one person and a strike on a communications facility in Dnipro. Continue reading...

Society & Human Rights.title: Badenoch says Tories want policies ‘for everybody’ as she defends plan to let millionaires get free childcare – UK politics live
Society & Human Rights.text: Conservative leader defends plan to extend free childcare to high earners, as Tory conference begins in Birmingham todayOn Friday the Times revealed that Katie Lam, the communities secretary, told a meeting in private earlier this year that the state pension system needs a fundamental overhaul.Speaking in June, when she was a frontbencher but not yet in the shadow cabinet, Lam was asked at a meeting with activists if she thought the pensions triple lock was sustainable. She replied:Ultimately I think what we will need in the end is an entirely new pension system.I mean, a baby that is born today has a 20% chance of living to be 100 and I don’t think we can fund one in five people half of their lives, you know, for the first 20 and the last 30 years. But obviously if you are 90 you probably can’t go out and get a job right, so I think you have to be realistic about how you would taper that and bring that in across the population.The fact is, the triple lock and pensions are things that people have contributed to.Conservatives believe that if you have contributed, then you deserve to get your state pension. Society & Human Rights.title: Thousands of Glasgow council workers face pay cuts in one of UK’s biggest fire-and-rehire plans
Society & Human Rights.text: Unison union refuses to ballot members on offer that would make 11% of council employees worse offUK politics live – latest updatesThousands of Glasgow council workers face being sacked and reappointed under less favourable terms in one of the UK’s biggest ever “fire-and-rehire” exercises, after union negotiations broke down once again this week.About 23,000 workers – all of the council’s non-teaching staff – first heard they were affected last week when talks between the SNP-led council and the GMB, Unison and Unite unions fell apart. Those negotiations concerned a new pay and grading system designed to resolve historical pay equality issues. Unison refused to ballot its members on an offer that would mean pay cuts for 11% of council employees, prompting the council to begin issuing fire-and-rehire letters. Continue reading...

Society & Human Rights.title: Feeling secure in a group may help dissenters make stronger arguments
Society & Human Rights.text: When everyone in a meeting voices the same opinion, an organization can miss important warning signs and new ideas. A research team from KAIST suggests that when members feel securely accepted within their group, they can express dissenting opinions in greater detail and more persuasively, and other members may be more willing to use those opinions in decision-making.

Society & Human Rights.title: Recovery after intimate partner violence: New study reveals what works

This type of violence is often perpetrated by a current or former partner, in which case it is referred to as intimate partner violence.

Cult Tokyo Label everyone Is Finally Coming to Hong Kong With a Temporary Brick-and-Mortar at BELOWGROUND
Entertainment.text: SummaryTokyo label everyone is making its first appearance in Hong Kong with a five-day pop-upTwo tees made only for the city, the ESS Tee and Vincent Logo LS Tee, headline the lineupPieces from A.PRESSE for everyone, adidas Originals, SUICOKE, Erik Schedin and Tomo Nariai fill out the racksTokyo label everyone is bringing its ESS Tee and Vincent Logo LS Tee to Hong Kong as part of its first pop-up in the city, and neither T-shirt will be sold anywhere else. Founded by Ryo Miyoshi, the brand has made its name on low-key staples where fabric and finish do the talking, and this visit gives local fans their first chance to shop it in person.The two exclusive T-shirts anchor the edit, and the rest of the space is a tight selection of everyone's everyday wardrobe. One standout is the label's easy slacks in Loro Piana fabric, a relaxed trouser in an upgraded material that sums up Miyoshi's approach well.Collaborations make up the next layer. Pieces from A.PRESSE for everyone will be on hand, a fitting addition since the pop-up sits a short walk from the A.Presse Dedicated Space by Gallery HBX in the same building. The label is also bringing its collaborative work with adidas Originals, SUICOKE, Erik Schedin and Tomo Nariai.The timing follows a busy year for the brand. everyone opened a flagship in Maebashi, Miyoshi's hometown, and an atelier in Seijo inside a building designed by Tadao Ando. Its second adidas Originals project put the label's own spin on the Adizero Adios OG runner, and everyone OOAK presented by Casa BRUTUS linked the brand with Min Hee-jin's ooak records.Not everything in the room is for sale. Miyoshi's taste for postmodern design shapes the space, with Ettore Sottsass's Carlton shelving unit, a piece Miyoshi counts among his most treasured, displayed next to Shiro Kuramata's Progetti Compiuti drawers for Cappellini."I’m very happy to bring everyone to Hong Kong for the first time. For me, everyone is about more than just clothes. It’s also about sharing the things we love and creating experiences together. I’m looking forward to meeting everyone in Hong Kong and sharing what we do in Tokyo," Miyoshi said in a statement.The everyone brick-and-mortar is open daily from October 9 to October 13 at BELOWGROUND Hong kong.everyone Temporary StoreShop B57-B58, BELOWGROUNDB1/F, Landmark Atrium15 Queen's Road Central, Hong KongOpening Hours: 10:30 a.m. to 7:30 p.m.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: BEAMS x Lacoste Turned the Iconic Crocodile Into a "BEAMS" Logo for the Label's 50th
Entertainment.text: SummaryBEAMS has teamed up with Lacoste on a matching Plaid Hooded Jacket and Plaid Pants as part of its 50th anniversary collaborationsBoth pieces use patterns made from scratch for the project, rather than reworked versions of existing Lacoste stylesA plaid built around Lacoste's sportswear look runs across both pieces, finished with a crocodile graphic spelling out "BEAMS"BEAMS and Lacoste have released a Plaid Hooded Jacket and Plaid Pants, a two-piece setup made to celebrate the Japanese retailer's 50th anniversary. Instead of putting a BEAMS label on an existing Lacoste design, the pair built both garments from the pattern up. They share a fabric and a print, so they can be worn as a full set or split up.The print is the main draw. The check is original to the collab, built around the clean, athletic look Lacoste is known for, and it runs across both the jacket and the pants. The other signature detail is a custom graphic that keeps the outline of Lacoste's crocodile emblem and works the "BEAMS" name into it.The jacket is a hooded blouson with a roomy, boxy cut, and the pants follow the same easygoing shape. Worn together, they read as a relaxed, sporty set made for weekends rather than anything tailored. The beige version leans warm and vintage, while the navy is the more understated of the two.The setup sits inside a larger BEAMS x Lacoste capsule that also includes a striped shirt, a long-sleeve polo in heavy piqué and a thermal T-shirt with a logo, all made for the anniversary.The BEAMS x Lacoste Plaid Hooded Jacket and Plaid Pants are available now via the BEAMS online store.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: Drake Is Reportedly in the Running to Headline Coachella 2027
Entertainment.text: SummaryDrake is reportedly under consideration as a headliner for Coachella 2027, according to music industry outlet 'HitsDailyDouble''A booking would mark his first time at the top of the bill since he closed out both Sundays of the 2015 editionThe rumored slot would sit alongside a world tour he has already confirmed for 2027Drake could be lining up a return to Coachella as one of the festival's 2027 headliners, according to a new report. On October 2, HitsDailyDouble said in its HitsList column, a regular roundup of music industry news and gossip, that the rapper is among the names being weighed for the top of next year's bill. Nothing has been confirmed, but the timing lines up neatly with one of the busiest stretches of his career.The report places Drake in early talks rather than in a finalized booking, so the details remain thin. If the slot comes together, it would mean two headlining performances across the festival's back-to-back weekends in Indio, California, adding to a 2027 calendar that already includes a world tour.The rumor comes on the back of a strong 2026. Drake released three albums this year — ICEMAN, MAID OF HONOUR and HABIBTI, and the first of them did most of the chart damage. ICEMAN opened at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 and held the top spot on the Billboard Canadian Albums chart for five weeks. He followed the album run in September with FOMO, an hour-long short film packed with unreleased songs, and four of those tracks reached streaming services on October 2 through the HABIBTI (FOMO) deluxe edition.His history at the festival gives the rumor extra weight. Drake last headlined Coachella in 2015, closing both Sunday nights roughly two months after the release of If You're Reading This It's Too Late. That set covered his whole catalog to that point, and it is still remembered for a surprise appearance from Madonna and the onstage kiss that followed. He returned in 2017, this time as a guest during Future's set, where the pair ran through a few songs including their collaboration "Jumpman."His recent festival work hints at what a 2027 set could look like. When he headlined Wireless Festival in London in 2025, Drake gave each of his three nights its own focus: one for his R&B catalog, one for straight hip-hop and one for his Caribbean-inspired records. His three 2026 albums were split along similar genre lines, which gives him plenty of material if he wants to build two different sets for the two Coachella weekends.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: Dickies x WACKO MARIA FW26 Unleash a Leopard Active Jacket on Your Workwear Rotation
Entertainment.text: SummaryWACKO MARIA and Dickies have lined up a three-piece capsule anchored by a leopard version of the Active Jacket in BeigeThe jacket also arrives in solid Black and Charcoal, with every version cut from 100% cottonPleated Trousers in a polyester and cotton blend complete the lineup across Black, Brown, Charcoal and IvoryWACKO MARIA and Dickies have released a new three-piece capsule led by the Leopard Active Jacket. The drop pairs two takes on the jacket with a set of Pleated Trousers, keeping the focus tight on a top-and-bottom workwear pairing.The Leopard Active Jacket is the statement piece of the set. It comes in a single Beige colorway, letting the animal motif do the talking against a neutral base, and is built entirely from cotton.For those who prefer their outerwear without the print, the standard Active Jacket keeps the same all-cotton makeup and trades the leopard for solid Black or Charcoal. The result is two distinct registers of the same garment: one loud, one built for everyday rotation.The Pleated Trousers shift the fabric story. Instead of pure cotton, they use a 65% polyester and 35% cotton blend, a mix that leans toward durability and easier care in a pant designed for daily wear. The pleated cut gives the trousers a dressier line than a standard work pant, and they have the widest palette in the capsule, available in Black, Brown, Charcoal and Ivory.Taken together, the colorways are designed to cross over. Both Black and Charcoal appear on the solid jacket and the trousers, making it easy to run the pieces as a matching set, while the Beige leopard jacket sits naturally over the Brown or Ivory trousers.The Dickies x WACKO MARIA capsule is available now via the WACKO MARIA online store, with worldwide shipping available.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: KEEN Turns Its Two-Cord UNEEK Into a Luxury Leather Mule
Entertainment.text: Name: KEEN UNEEK Mule WKColorway: BlackSKU: 1033311MSRP: $195 USDRelease Date: October 2Where to Buy: KeenKEEN is taking its most recognizable design in a more refined direction with the All Gender UNEEK Mule WK. The shoe converts the brand's iconic two-cord sneaker into an ultra-premium mule, handcrafted in ethically sourced leather and finished in black.The core idea is a change in form. The UNEEK's defining two-cord construction carries over, but the closed sneaker becomes a mule, with the back opened up for an easy slip-on fit. Keeping the cords while removing the heel means the silhouette stays instantly recognizable even as it moves into a more relaxed shape.The material shift is just as significant. Instead of the technical build associated with the original model, the mule is handcrafted from ethically sourced leather. That choice, together with the handwork, is what moves the UNEEK from a trail-adjacent oddity into the premium category KEEN is targeting here. The all-black finish keeps the focus on the leather and the cordwork rather than on color.The move also fits the UNEEK's history. The silhouette first arrived in 2014, and its open, cord-built design has always stood apart from the hiking boots and water sandals that make up most of KEEN's catalog. That outlier status helped it win fans beyond the outdoors crowd. A leather mule leans into that identity, presenting the UNEEK as a design object first and outdoor gear second.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: White Mountaineering x Umbro's Fourth Capsule Is Cut From H2OFF Taffeta and Archive Lines
Entertainment.text: SummaryWhite Mountaineering and UMBRO have released their fourth collaboration, a three-piece capsule rooted in UMBRO's archiveThe hooded jacket and easy pants share H2OFF polyester taffeta construction and fluid paneling across four matching colorwaysA crewneck pullover rounds out the drop with front co-branding, UV protection, and a cool-to-the-touch finishWhite Mountaineering and Umbro have returned with their fourth collaboration, a focused three-piece capsule led by a hooded jacket and easy pants made from H2OFF polyester taffeta. Both pieces start from Umbro archive designs, and White Mountaineering's rework shows most clearly in the fabric and the paneling.H2OFF is the technical backbone of the capsule. The high-performance polyester taffeta forms both the hooded jacket and the easy pants, giving the two archive-derived silhouettes a shared material base. The source doesn't list the fabric's specific performance claims, so its exact function is best confirmed with the brand.The design work lives in the paneling. Rather than reproducing Umbro’s archive pieces as they were, the collaboration breaks up their surfaces with fluid, flowing panel lines, trading the rigid blocking typical of sportswear for something more organic. The jacket and pants come in the same four colorways (black, khaki, green, and gray), so the matching fabric and palette let them be worn as a coordinated set or split apart.The crewneck pullover handles the function-first side of the drop. It carries both brands' logos across the front and adds UV protection alongside a cool-to-the-touch finish, which makes it a lighter layer suited to warmer days in transitional weather. Its palette narrows to black, khaki, and charcoal, with charcoal standing in for the green and gray offered on the jacket and pants.The White Mountaineering x Umbro capsule is available now through White Mountaineering stores, select stockists, and the White Mountaineering online store.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: Milly Alcock Is the 'Supergirl' That Makes Sense
Entertainment.text: Superhero films have been trying to figure out Supergirl for decades. The 1984 Helen Slater version arrived at the tail end of the Christopher Reeve era and felt inherited rather than earned. The character has cycled through TV iterations and animated appearances since, each one orbiting Superman's mythology without ever establishing a gravitational pull of its own. The problem was never Kara Zor-El. The problem was that nobody had quite worked out who she actually was, underneath the cape.Craig Gillespie's 2026 film, based on Tom King and Bilquis Evely's acclaimed comic run, at least understands the question. This version of Kara is not the wide-eyed, optimistic cousin of Kal-El that popular culture has defaulted to for years. She is something considerably more complicated: a woman who watched Krypton die, who spent years in survival mode before landing on a planet that already had a Superman and therefore didn't quite know what to do with her, and who has been carrying the weight of that displacement ever since. When James Gunn described her as "much more hardcore" than previous versions, that wasn't marketing language. It was a genuine reorientation of the character.Milly Alcock carries all of that without making it feel like a burden the film is dragging behind it. Her Kara is guarded and occasionally reckless and capable of a warmth she doesn't entirely know how to express, and Alcock moves between those registers with a naturalness that the writing doesn't always support but her performance does regardless. She emerged from House of the Dragon with a reputation for playing young women navigating impossible circumstances with more composure than anyone around them deserves, and she brings exactly that quality here. The suit fits. More importantly, the character fits.The film's aesthetic leans hard into the source material's cosmic brutalism, all alien landscapes and red sun light and a grungier visual grammar that has more in common with the Furiosa end of the spectrum than anything the MCU has produced. It is not always elegant, and the cinematography makes some choices that prioritize mood over clarity in ways that don't always pay off. But the ambition behind the aesthetic is coherent, which is more than can be said for most superhero films operating at this scale.The relationship between Kara and Ruthye, the young girl whose revenge mission drives the film's plot, gives Alcock something to work against, and the dynamic between them is where the film finds its emotional footing. Ruthye's bluntness and Kara's reluctant protectiveness produce a texture that straightforward hero-versus-villain structures rarely allow.Supergirl will not be everyone's entry point into the new DCU, and it carries the uneven energy of a franchise still working out its own internal logic. But Alcock makes a case for this character that has never been made before with quite this much conviction. Whatever the DCU builds around her next, the foundation is there.Supergirl is available now on Cathay Pacific‘s award-winning inflight entertainment system.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: PUMA GOLF x Saturdays NYC Spot the Clyde Golf in Leopard for Round Two
Entertainment.text: SummaryPUMA GOLF and Saturdays NYC have reunited for a second capsule built around a leopard-print edition of the PUMA Clyde GolfFive apparel pieces use the print at different volumes, from an all-over sweater to trousers that reveal it only at the pocketsThe lineup pairs the footwear with a reversible vest, a long-sleeve polo, and a cap for a full on-course kitPUMA GOLF and Saturdays NYC have returned for a second collaboration, anchored by a leopard-print take on the PUMA Clyde Golf. The capsule runs six pieces, one pair of shoes and five apparel items, and treats the animal print as its connecting thread rather than a one-off accent.The footwear is the centerpiece. The Clyde Golf is PUMA's course-ready reworking of the Clyde, one of the brand's defining silhouettes, and this edition brings leopard print onto the shoe. It turns a familiar profile into something that reads louder on the green, while the golf-specific update keeps the shoe grounded in its purpose.The apparel is where the print gets tuned up and down. A long-sleeve sweater is the boldest piece, rendered in leopard, while a reversible vest gives the wearer two looks from one layer. The source doesn't specify which side carries the print, so the vest's exact configuration is worth checking against product imagery.Elsewhere, the capsule shows more restraint. The two-tuck pants keep the pattern hidden until the pockets open, where a flash of leopard shows through, a quieter detail that rewards a closer look. A long-sleeve polo carries a logo at the chest, and a cap completes the lineup, giving the collection a head-to-toe option for players who want the print on the whole kit.The PUMA GOLF x Saturdays NYC capsule releases October 2 in Japan. It will be available through Saturdays NYC stores and the Saturdays NYC online store, the PUMA Store Harajuku, Osaka, and Fukuoka, the PUMA online store. and the PUMA app.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: Tiny Hotels Are Luxury Travel’s Next Big Thing
Entertainment.text: Bloomberg Pursuits reporter Sarah Rappaport tells Bloomberg This Weekend that luxury travelers are increasingly seeking tiny hotels with as few as one to six rooms, combining the privacy of a villa with personalized high-end hotel service. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Rappaport says the trend is spreading across Europe and the US as travelers seek exclusivity, fewer crowds and unusual experiences in restaurants, museums and historic properties. Science & Technology.title: Reading hidden topology in light, even when energy leaks away
Science & Technology.text: When I explain topology to students, I start with a knot in a rope. You can stretch it, twist it or shake it, but the knot stays until you cut the rope. Physicists have found that some materials and devices carry similar "knots" in how waves move through them. These are topological properties, labeled by whole numbers that don't change under small imperfections. That robustness is why topology has become one of the central ideas in modern physics. It promises electronics, photonics and quantum devices that tolerate defects and noise.

Science & Technology.title: iGarden's K70 AI Pool Cleaner Takes Pool Duty Off Your Summer To-Do List
Science & Technology.text: SummaryFairland Group's outdoor tech arm iGarden has brought its K70 AI Pool Cleaner to Australia just as backyard swim season ramps upAn AI-Inverter system tunes power output to pool conditions, letting the unit run for up to 16 days before it needs rechargingTurbo 200% suction, 22,000 LPH of water flow and a two-stage filter pull in everything from fallen leaves to fine dustiGarden has launched the K70 AI Pool Cleaner in Australia, a robotic cleaner built to take the weekly grind out of pool upkeep. The release comes from Fairland Group's outdoor technology division and lands as the country heads into its warmer months, when backyard pools shift from seasonal fixture to the center of family life and weekend gatherings.The K70 runs on AI-Inverter technology, which reads the state of the pool and dials its power up or down to match. That adaptive approach is what allows the cleaner to keep working for up to 16 days on one charge, so owners can leave it in the water for stretches of the season instead of pulling it out to plug in every few sessions.Coverage is just as thorough. Intelligent navigation guides the unit across the different surfaces of a residential pool, so it reaches the steps, climbs the walls, sweeps the floor and works along the waterline, where grime tends to build up first. The goal is a full-pool clean in one pass rather than a floor-only sweep that leaves the edges to a net and brush.Suction comes from iGarden's Turbo 200% technology paired with water flow rated at up to 22,000 LPH, enough to handle large debris like leaves alongside much finer particles. Everything it picks up passes through a two-stage filter. A 180 μm outer layer catches the bigger material while a 50 μm inner layer traps the fine stuff, and a 4-litre collection basket means fewer stops to empty it mid-clean.Controls stay simple. Instead of routing every setting through a companion app, the K70 places a touchscreen directly on the body of the device, putting its functions within reach at the poolside. For Australian households that treat the backyard as an extension of the living room, the pitch is clear: let the machine handle the scrubbing and spend the summer in the water instead.The iGarden K70 AI Pool Cleaner is available now in Australia via the iGarden Official Store.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast
